purpose: Pre-fit frozen development ablations; not a confirmatory novelty or operational reliability claim

experiments.E1: Generic event text versus semantic event text versus semantic event plus bounded prior entity context
experiments.E2: Random record loss, contiguous support loss and removal of command-record types; compare ordinary versus dropout-augmented training
experiments.E3: Delayed command records at shared 0, 30 and 120 second deadlines; measure accuracy and coverage at each deadline

ait.role: Previously exposed eight-run development data; regrouped audit-event task

casino.role: Recent RAID2025 second source; technique versus other annotated technique, not benign detection
casino.prediction_unit: First observed audit event per source process-technique annotation and host; deduplicate event IDs and union overlapping labels. Other events can provide prior context but are not eligible training/scoring targets. This annotation-onset proxy is not independently established malicious-action onset.

cohort.selection: All author-annotated instances, SHA256(casino-robustness-v1:instance) sorted order
cohort.reason: The initial24-instance feasibility sample had no T1068 and one T1548 test annotation. Expanded before any Casino model fit or outcome inspection, using all available annotated instances rather than selecting favorable cases.
cohort.support_note: These are annotation inventory counts, not final deduplicated event targets or independent attacks.

history.entity_keys: Only keys explicitly present in currently visible target and prior fragments; run and host scoped. No label inputs.

metadata_features: Only observed record counts, record types, context count and context age; no true deletion mask or attacker identifiers

dropout_training.sample_weight_per_view: 1 divided by number of views, preserving total clean training weight and effective regularization
dropout_training.empty_view_prediction: forced no alarm in every arm

perturbation_scope: Random removal applies consistently to current and prior record fragments. Support burst removes only preceding 60 seconds at each target query, a targeted stress test rather than a shared physical outage. Channel removal is audit record-type removal, not a whole sensor outage.
decision_time: Target event timestamp plus common deadline. Only fragments whose simulated availability <= deadline and source timestamp <= target event time; no later source events. Native fragment arrival times are not measured.
delay_interpretation: At deadline >= injected deterministic delay, the clean view is restored by construction. Recovery is a buffering/replay control with a latency cost, not evidence of a learned robustness improvement.
empty_targets: Retain target in denominators, score 0, force no alarm, report observed-target coverage. Offline source-event roster is evaluator knowledge, not a deployable event trigger.

calibration.source: Clean calibration only, separately for each model and target; frozen across perturbations
calibration.interpretation: Other-label event flag rate, not verified benign false alarms or a population bound

target_support: Require both classes in fit, calibration and test; otherwise report unsupported without training target. Counts are correlated events, not independent attacks.
success_interpretation: Report paired per-run changes and actual flag burden at each common deadline. Three removal seeds characterize perturbation variability only. No significance claim from row resampling; no cherry-picked seed or target; absence of improvement closes the tested control, not all context methods.
novelty: Representation repair, event grouping, history features and dropout are existing controls. A distinct research contribution requires a further mechanism and external confirmation.
cohort_amendment: AIT results are already exposed development evidence. Its original protocol and saved results remain unchanged. This separate protocol changes only Casino cohort qualification; classifier, feature, loss, seed and metric settings are unchanged.
